task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of July 15, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer answering why a laundromat's electricity bill can fall even when its monthly energy use stays the same, using the supplied demand-charge records.

facts.text: Arden Wash's May and June 2026 bills from Cobalt Municipal Power both show 5,000 kilowatt-hours of electricity use.
Its commercial tariff charges $20 monthly, 12 cents per kilowatt-hour and $9 per kilowatt of billed peak demand.
The energy-use charge was therefore $600 in both months.
Billed peak demand fell from 60 kilowatts in May to 45 in June, reducing the demand charge from $540 to $405.
The stated electricity charges totaled $1,160 in May and $1,025 in June, a $135 difference.
These totals exclude separately itemized taxes, which are not supplied for the comparison.
The tariff measures billed demand using the highest 15-minute average load during weekday 4-7 p.m. windows in the billing month.
Kilowatt-hours describe accumulated electricity use, while the billed kilowatts describe the rate of use during a particular peak interval.
Owner Mara Selt installed timers to stagger the start of several large dryers instead of starting them together.
The bills show lower demand after that change but do not isolate every difference in weather, customers or machine use between months.
Staggering machines can spread electricity use across time without eliminating the energy required for each completed load.
Selt said some customers prefer starting several loads together because they have limited time at the laundromat.
Selt said, "The meter rewards spreading things out. A customer may need to be finished before the bus leaves."
Utility analyst Oren Quill said a single busy interval can set the demand charge for the month.
Quill said, "The bill remembers the busiest quarter-hour, even after the machines have gone quiet."
The utility offers a reading of past interval data but does not guarantee a business will reproduce its lowest demand next month.
Cobalt's residential tariff does not include this commercial demand charge.
The laundromat's lease includes no automatic rent reduction for lower electricity bills.
Arden Wash has operated in the same storefront since 2008 and provides both self-service and staffed washing.
The supplied bills do not establish a carbon-emissions saving from using the same monthly energy at different times.

forbidden_additions: A reduction in the stated monthly kilowatt-hours or a guaranteed future bill
Identical household charges, included taxes or a quantified emissions benefit
